# Manage grant spending and reporting

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

After accepting a grant, subsidy or reimbursable innovation award. Reconciled eligible spending, accepted reports and a controlled award closeout or remediation plan.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Translate the signed award into a control register

agent-runnable


Extract project dates, approved cost categories, matching funds, procurement rules, milestones and report requirements. Record sponsor approvals and amendments as the source of truth for the specific award.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve budget ownership and spending controls

human · human approval required


Finance and the project lead establish cost codes, time records, purchasing approval and evidence retention. Resolve restrictions with the sponsor before committing costs whose eligibility is uncertain.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Reconcile project expenditure and progress

agent-runnable


Match payroll, invoices, procurement and project outputs to the award budget and supporting records. Keep ineligible, disputed and unspent amounts separate and investigate variances before preparing a claim.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Authorize reports, claims and change requests

human · human approval required


The responsible signatory reviews the narrative, cost claim and certifications before delivery. Request required scope or budget changes through the sponsor process instead of assuming an internal reallocation is permitted.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Close the award and retain audit evidence

agent-runnable


Reconcile sponsor payments, adjustments, final reports and remaining obligations. Track unaccepted deliverables or possible repayments with an owner, and retain the evidence according to the award and applicable retention rules.

- Verify: Reconciled eligible spending, accepted reports and a controlled award closeout or remediation plan.
- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)
